edges.description: Disease-associated variants severely reduce GBA2 catalytic activity.
Reduced GBA2 hydrolysis raises glucosylceramide in patient cells.
Experimental systems connect GBA2 loss to altered actin dynamics, impaired neurite extension, and abnormal motor-axon morphology, but the lipid-to-cytoskeleton intermediates remain unresolved.
Cataract, hypogonadism, and skeletal deformity accompany the neurologic syndrome, but their intervening cell and tissue mechanisms are unknown.

edges.description: Long-tract, cerebellar, and peripheral-neural dysfunction produces the combined spastic-ataxia syndrome and associated imaging findings.
Cerebellar circuit dysfunction manifests as progressive ataxia.
Corticospinal involvement manifests as progressive lower-limb spastic paraparesis.
Peripheral nerve involvement is frequent but variably ascertained.
Cognitive impairment is common and may emerge late.
Cerebellar atrophy is a variable rather than obligatory imaging correlate.
A thin or atrophic corpus callosum is a frequent but inconsistent MRI finding.
White-matter abnormalities occur in a minority overall but were prominent in the recent Italian series.
Limb or cranial dystonia is part of the variable movement-disorder spectrum.
Head or limb tremor occurs in a subset.
Upper-gaze palsy is an occasional and potentially identifying ocular-motor feature.
Neurogenic bladder symptoms, particularly urgency or urge incontinence, occur variably.
Bilateral cataracts can create a Marinesco-Sjögren-like presentation.
